Header:
Date: 2026-03-16
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~45 mins
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendez (Acme Head of ML Ops), Sana Patel (Acme Platform Eng), Liam O'Connor (Acme CTO)

Summary (auto): Weekly POC sync focused on benchmark results comparing Redwood to their current baseline provider. Discussed p95/p50 latency, throughput (QPS), quantization and batching tradeoffs, VPC/security questions, and next steps to run additional experiments.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for making time, we'll kick off the weekly sync. Quick roll call, then Priya will walk through the updated numbers.
[00:12] Carlos: Yep, Carlos here. We pulled in some extra logs overnight so hopefully more realistic numbers.
[00:18] Sana: Sana present.
[00:20] Liam: Liam here, sorry I'm on a bit delayed.
[00:23] Jordan: No worries. Priya, over to you.
[00:30] Priya: Cool thanks. So, we ran the benchmark suite against your baseline provider (what you sent over) and against a few Redwood configs. I uploaded the spreadsheet to the shared folder - link in the invite, titled "acme-bench-20260316.xlsx". High level, at the default FP16 model: Redwood median latencies were ~120ms, p95 ~320ms, throughput ~28 QPS for the 1k token sequence simulated load. BaselineAI numbers were median 180ms, p95 520ms, throughput ~18 QPS.
[01:05] Sana: That's a pretty big gap at p95, is that stable across runs?
[01:10] Priya: There is run-to-run variance, but we saw consistent 30-40% improvement in p95 across the 10+ runs. Our continuous batching and KV cache hit rates improved tail latency. Also note we pinned instance types to the same NVIDIA family where possible but kernel selection differs so that affects perf.
[01:30] Carlos: Quick Q: are those numbers from hosted or dedicated config? We need to know since Acme plans to go private later.
[01:36] Priya: These were on a dedicated pool mirror (equivalent capacity) to keep apples-to-apples. For hosted we saw similar medians but slightly higher p95 under bursty traffic.
[01:48] Jordan: Also worth flagging we tested a quantized 4-bit profile; that increased throughput to ~42 QPS but p95 tightened only to ~360ms, and we saw minor decoding artifacts in 2% of responses on edge-case prompts. That's the quality tradeoff.
[02:10] Liam: That decoding artifacts — can you describe? Is it hallucination or garbled tokens?
[02:14] Priya: Mostly tokenization artifacts and occasional short truncations on very long context windows. Not semantic hallucination, more like occasional repeated tokens. We can tune sampling and decode fallback to reduce that.
[02:26] Sana: For our use case (search re-ranking + summarization), even small truncations are problematic. We need to see end-to-end quality numbers.
[02:34] Jordan: Understood. We'll attach the eval prompts you provided and Priya will run the quantized config specifically with your summarization set and report rouge/accuracy delta.
[02:43] Priya: Yep, I added the eval column in the spreadsheet and will run the quality checks.
[02:48] Jordan: On throughput — you mentioned peak QPS during Black Friday-like load. Carlos, what peak are we planning for?
[02:54] Carlos: Our expected peak is ~120 QPS sustained for ~10 minutes with spikes to 200 QPS for a couple of minutes. That's why we care about autoscale and burst options.
[03:04] Priya: We validated autoscale up to 3x of baseline in the dedicated pool and saw linear scaling in throughput; cold scale-up adds ~45s which we can mitigate with warm pools.
[03:14] Carlos: Any risk with KV cache invalidation when scaling? We've had issues where cache warming caused tail latency spikes.
[03:20] Priya: Good call — cache warming is an issue. Our recommendation: keep a small warm standby and preload popular prefixes; also use sticky routing during scale events. We'll provide config snippets.
[03:32] Liam: Security — are audit logs and KMS integration available in the dedicated/private deployment? We need to ensure no keys are leaving our environment.
[03:40] Jordan: Yes, Private includes customer-managed KMS/HSM and audit logs. For the Dedicated flow we offer optional private control plane and VPC peering. We'll put together a short doc comparing Dedicated vs Private for your compliance checklist.
[03:53] Sana: We have SOC2 and GDPR constraints; is Redwood SOC2 Type II certified?
[03:58] Jordan: Yes, Redwood is SOC2 Type II and we also have ISO attestation in region. I'll share the compliance pack.
[04:05] Priya: Back to benchmarks — we also ran an experiment with dynamic batching tuned to your sequence length distribution (avg 600 tokens). That gave about 20% throughput uplift without quality hit.
[04:16] Carlos: Nice. Can we get the exact batch size and latency tradeoffs? We need to replicate.
[04:20] Priya: In the spreadsheet I left a note: batch target 64, latency SLO at p95 stayed under 350ms. But that'll vary with prompt variability.
[04:28] Jordan: I'll call out the specific cell.
[04:31] Speaker 1 (probably Jordan): Also, we noticed BaselineAI had higher variance when sequence length spiked; their kernel selection didn't handle long attention efficiently.
[04:41] Carlos: Did you capture GPU utilization? That's a cost signal for us.
[04:44] Priya: Yes, attached a tab with utilization — Redwood averaged 78% GPU util, BaselineAI 92% for the same throughput, meaning Baseline is less efficient (higher cost per token).
[04:56] Sana: Do you have cost-per-1M tokens estimate? We need to compare.
[05:00] Jordan: We put a normalized cost row — Redwood came in ~30% lower cost per token after batching + KV cache assumed; numbers are in the sheet but we'll annotate assumptions (instance pricing, preemptible vs reserved).
[05:12] Carlos: Good. On operations, how easy is model rollback if we see a regression post-deploy?
[05:18] Priya: Rollbacks are simple — we support model version pinning and can do canary and automatic fallback to baseline model if regressions are detected by your eval set. We'll demo that in the next session.
[05:29] Liam: For our timeline, we want a short pilot for production readiness in 6 weeks, then dedicated contract. Is that feasible?
[05:36] Jordan: Yes that's within normal POC cadence. First two weeks finish remaining perf/quality experiments, then production smoke tests, then pilot. We'll map milestones.
[05:44] Sana: One last thing — network egress and data residency. We'll need region-specific deployment. Can Redwood guarantee region placement?
[05:52] Jordan: Yes, we can pin deployments to regions; for Private you can run fully on-prem. We'll add region mapping to the doc.
[05:59] Carlos: Ok, thanks.
[06:01] Jordan: Recap of action items: Jordan shares updated sheet; Priya runs quantized quality checks and batching configs; Carlos provides production corpus. We'll sync next Tuesday same time. Anything else?
[06:12] Sana: No, that's it.
[06:14] Liam: Thanks all.
[06:16] Jordan: Great, meeting adjourned.
